clue.text: Post application at once, I'd say

indicators.note: the setter announces how the phrase is spoken, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: right off means immediately, at once

explanation.surface: Someone urging that a postal application be sent immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post application' is read literally: applying by post is to write off for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To write off is to apply by letter, so posting a request is exactly that act.

clue.text: Delight about author reciting

parts.note: re is the crossword word for about, concerning

indicators.note: a recitation is spoken, so the name is taken as it sounds

parts.note: James Joyce, the Irish author of Ulysses

explanation.surface: A reader takes pleasure in hearing a writer read their work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delight' reads as a noun but is the verb; the author is James Joyce, the Irish novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejoice is to delight, be glad; both are verbs of taking pleasure.

clue.text: Game played by two of Turandot's DEV ministers?

definitions.text: Game played by two of Turandot's DEV ministers?

parts.words: Game played by two of Turandot's DEV ministers?
parts.note: the three ministers in Puccini's opera Turandot are Ping, Pang and Pong; two of them together name the game's nickname

explanation.surface: A question about pastimes in Puccini's opera Turandot.
explanation.walkthrough: Ping and Pong together give ping-pong, the familiar name for the game. 'DEV' looks like a stray OCR fragment and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: Ping-pong is the everyday name for the indoor bat-and-ball game played across a net on a board.

clue.text: Nothing to read in this language

parts.note: O, the zero shape, is nothing
to scan a text is to read it

explanation.surface: A complaint that a language has no literature at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The language is an ancient Italic tongue of southern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: It was an ancient Italic language spoken in Campania before Latin replaced it.

clue.text: Iron, good in the bone

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
moral means good, virtuous

explanation.surface: A nutritional note that iron is good for the bones.
explanation.definitionFit: Femoral describes what relates to the thigh bone, the femur, so it is a matter in the bone.

clue.text: Blue needed by country missing a game

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the named letter is dropped

parts.note: India is a country
Go is a Japanese board game

explanation.surface: A national team in blue that needs one more match.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep blue dye and colour.

clue.text: Several Edmunds in Cromwell's army

definitions.meaning: Edmund Ironside was an English king in 1016, so more than one of him
Oliver Cromwell's cavalry troopers in the English Civil War were given this nickname

explanation.definitionFit: The plural of the Saxon king's byname and the name given to Cromwell's Civil War soldiers coincide.

clue.text: Almost excessively be fond of girl

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: to dote is to be excessively fond

explanation.surface: A suitor who is a little too devoted to a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Dot is a girl's name, short for Dorothy.

clue.text: Kill in furious rage, too much to suppress

indicators.note: suppress here means hold down within, so one piece goes inside
furious suggests wild disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: OTT is over the top, too much

explanation.surface: A killing in a fit of excessive fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in furious rage' feels like part of the definition, but 'Kill' alone defines; OTT, short for over the top, is everyday British slang for excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: To garotte is to kill by strangling with a cord or wire.

clue.text: Tasks one arriving with capture of stronghold: no relief from this source

parts.note: jobs are tasks

indicators.note: capturing something takes it inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a comer is one who arrives
a fort is a stronghold

explanation.surface: A military report on duties and the seizure of a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: From the Book of Job, whose friends' consolation only made matters worse.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who claims to console but only makes distress worse is a source offering no relief.

clue.text: French author working as judge

parts.note: Andre Gide was a French novelist
on means working, functioning

explanation.surface: A French writer serving as a magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'judge' is a Biblical judge here, not a court official.
explanation.definitionFit: Gideon was one of the judges of Israel in the Old Testament Book of Judges.

clue.text: Artist impossible to resist

indicators.note: impossible suggests something out of order, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A painter whose charm cannot be resisted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impossible' rearranges the letters of TO RESIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante Gabriel Rossetti was a Pre-Raphaelite painter, so an example of a painter.

clue.text: Stretcher! It's clean, bad break

indicators.note: break means smash into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cry about a stretcher that is clean but badly broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber loop is something that stretches, so it is a stretcher in a playful sense.

clue.text: Town named after historian? Daughter's confused

indicators.note: after means following, so the town word comes behind the historian

parts.note: the Venerable Bede was an Anglo-Saxon historian
ville is French for town
D is the abbreviation for daughter; the 's is a link meaning has

explanation.surface: A muddled daughter asking about a town named for a historian.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedevilled means beset and confounded, troubled into confusion.

clue.text: Fancied being in a line, receiving bearers minute, of gifts

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Fancied being in a line, receiving bearers minute, of gifts' has the intruding word 'minute' splitting 'bearers of gifts' (MAGI); I+(MAGI)+N+A+RY needs the clue without it, and the scan is blank
annotationWithheld.clue: Fancied being in a line, receiving bearers minute, of gifts

clue.text: Magwitch gives a short signal

indicators.note: short means cut, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a bell is a signal

explanation.surface: A Dickens convict briefly gives a sign.
explanation.walkthrough: Abel Magwitch is the convict in Dickens's Great Expectations.
explanation.definitionFit: Magwitch's first name in Great Expectations is Abel, so the surname defines the forename.

clue.text: People generally addressed in the country

parts.note: O is the vocative used to address someone, as in O king
man means people in general, mankind

explanation.surface: A speech to the people of a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Oman is a country on the Arabian Peninsula.

clue.text: Complain about this Roman elevated style

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to moan is to complain
hic is Latin, a Roman's word, for this

explanation.surface: Grumbling about a Roman's lofty manner.
explanation.definitionFit: The hairstyle is a raised central strip of hair, a style that literally stands up.

clue.text: Sackville-West taken back in charge in case

indicators.note: in means placed within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: to accuse is to charge

indicators.note: taken back means turned round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: Vita Sackville-West was an English writer and gardener

explanation.surface: Vita Sackville-West rearrested on a charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken back' turns VITA into ATIV, which goes 'in' ACCUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The accusative is a grammatical case, that of the direct object.

clue.text: During tea, different sort of bun offered

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece sits inside

parts.note: cha is tea
else means other, different

explanation.surface: At teatime, a new kind of bun is handed round.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chelsea bun is a rolled currant bun, so it names a kind of bun.

clue.text: Extreme north shown in colour

indicators.note: shown in means placed within, so one letter goes inside

parts.note: violet is a colour
N is north

explanation.surface: The far north shown in a particular colour on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent can mean intense or extreme, as in a violent contrast.

clue.text: Whip is available in white

indicators.note: in means placed within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: white means pure, chaste

explanation.surface: A whip available in white.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise is to punish, especially by beating, hence to whip.

clue.text: Area of dry hill

parts.note: sec is French for dry, used of wine
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A description of a parched hilly region.
explanation.definitionFit: A sector is a part or area, as of a city or field of activity.

clue.text: Take illegal drug and a little whisky

definitions.meaning: to sniff a drug such as cocaine up the nose
a small drink, a nip or dram

explanation.definitionFit: Snorting cocaine is inhaling it; a snort is also slang for a quick drink.

clue.text: Sacred island, note, beyond range? That's pitiful

indicators.note: beyond means after, so the following pieces come behind

parts.note: compass means range, scope
Iona is the Hebridean island where St Columba founded his monastery
te is a note in sol-fa

explanation.surface: A remark that a holy island is out of reach, which is a pity.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitiful in its old sense means full of pity, which is what compassionate means.

clue.text: Mark a page in guide

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for the German mark currency

explanation.surface: Advice to mark a page in a guidebook.
explanation.definitionFit: A map is a guide to finding one's way.

clue.text: Babywear put on son: make it fast, so

indicators.note: put on a boy, the babywear sits beside the son letter, behind it

parts.note: S is son
a nappy is what a baby wears; British for diaper

explanation.surface: Instructions to get a nappy on a boy quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make it fast' is a hint that 'make it snappy' means hurry up.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom make it snappy means be quick, so the word fills the blank as fast.

clue.text: Remedy is neat solution covering one spot

indicators.note: covering means going around, so another piece is held inside
solution means dissolving, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a dot is a spot

explanation.surface: A neat lotion to treat a single pimple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solution' rearranges NEAT to ANTE, and 'covering' puts IDOT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote is a remedy that counteracts poison.
